trial_court: Administrative Civil Judge (Central), Delhi - Petition No. 527/2004
case_name: Smt. Raj @ Usha vs The State & Ors

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Raj @ Usha, widow and mother of minors Jyotika, Deepak, Priyanka, Deepika, Suraj, Monica, Aakash

facts_of_case: Petitioner Smt. Raj @ Usha and her seven minor children seek succession certificate for debts and securities left behind by deceased Jagmal Singh, who died on 13.12.2003.

legal_principles.principle: A second marriage while the first marriage is subsisting is void.
legal_principles.held: The legal proportion in this regard is well settled that as per provisions of Hindu Marriage Act that 'Until the first marriage is dissolved or the earlier spouse dies, no Hindu can marry again'.

legal_principles.principle: A nominee is merely a trustee and receiving hand who receives securities on behalf of the actual successor.
legal_principles.held: The law is well settled that the nominee is merely a trustee and a receiving hand who receives the securities on behalf of actual successor.

legal_principles.principle: Children born from void marriages have equal right to inheritance.
legal_principles.held: The children born from the void marriages as well as the adopted son from first marriage will have equal right, inheritance of the assets of the deceased.

legal_principles.principle: Second marriage performed with the consent of earlier spouse is still void.
legal_principles.held: Even if such a second marriage is performed with the consent of earlier spouse, still the second marriage would be void.

outcome.final_order: The trial court granted the petitioners' request for a succession certificate.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for succession certificate
advising on Hindu Marriage Act implications
